problems: DECISION: the six Australian colonies and New Zealand are drawn as legal jurisdiction (letters patent lines), not effective control; Cliopatria's British Colonial Empire row draws only settled land (7 cells of Australia in 1788, 675 in 1850, 19,472 in 1880). If the renderer wants effective control the colony shapes must shrink and the interior become nobody's land. Details in the notes file and each dossier's notes.

OVERLAPS: Cliopatria's British Colonial Empire (eu-11) still draws Australia, New Zealand, Fiji (70 of 83 cells in 1980) and the Solomons (78 cells in 1980); the German Empire row draws 810 cells of Papua New Guinea in 1890-1910; the United States row (am-07) contains districts of the trust territory until 1986. The colony dossiers should replace those cells on the ledger dates.

empire-of-japan (jk-01) should use counterparts german-new-guinea (1914, 1920), south-seas-mandate, british-solomon-islands-protectorate (1942-1945), gilbert-and-ellice-islands (1941-1943) and territory-of-nauru (Aug 1942-Sep 1945) for its occupation and gain events.

new-zealand (oc-02-a): Tokelau 1925 gain has a guessed counterpart (kingdom-of-great-britain); the Gilbert and Ellice Islands page says 11 February 1926 (administration) and 1948 (sovereignty), so the counterpart is gilbert-and-ellice-islands. new-zealand records cook-islands (1965) and niue (1974) as vassal clients and those states now have their own dossiers: do not draw the land twice.

kingdom-of-fiji (oc-01) ends 1874-10 with counterpart british-colonial-empire; colony-of-fiji is the state that takes the land. kingdom-of-samoa (oc-01) ends 1900-02 with counterpart german-empire; german-samoa is the state that takes the German part from March 1900.

Scope: 25 dossiers were written against an aim of 6-10: the first 15 are the colonies and territories with land; the last 10 (samoa, nauru, territory-of-nauru, tuvalu, kiribati, republic-of-the-marshall-islands, cook-islands, niue, commonwealth-of-the-northern-mariana-islands, colony-of-norfolk-island) were added because sibling dossiers name them as counterparts or successors (Nauru because german-new-guinea otherwise left it without a successor). german-new-guinea, gilbert-and-ellice-islands, trust-territory-of-the-pacific-islands and colony-of-tasmania were re-published mid-run (Nauru events; notes only for the other three).

Page budget: colony-of-new-zealand used nine pages (four over the 2-5 budget; four are one-fact pages); the micro-states used one page each (one to nine grid cells). Territorial_evolution_of_New_Zealand returned URL not found; the Colony_of_Western_Australia URL redirected to the History of Western Australia article.

Accessed dates: Colony of New South Wales, Territorial evolution of Australia, Colony of Victoria and Colony of Queensland were fetched across midnight UTC and are recorded as 2026-10-18; all later pages 2026-10-19.

Conventions: living states end in 2024 (Cliopatria's last year; the schema says the current year); wikidata is null in every dossier (ids are not on the pages and were not taken from memory); type colony is used for dependencies of a metropole (UK colonies family britain, German colonies germany, South Seas Mandate japan, TTPI and Northern Mariana Islands americas).

Non-state belligerents (Maori hapu forces, Wiradjuri, Kalkadoon, Aboriginal Tasmanians, Ballarat miners and similar) are plain names in wars and counterparts; none is a state held for ten years, so no dossier is requested. The gazetteer's Marshall Is. shape is two cells near Majuro only.

Page disagreements are listed per state in the notes file (Queensland creation date, Western Australia founding date, Norfolk Island 1844 transfer day, Nauru mandate year and 1888 protectorate, Japanese landing at Nauru 25 or 26 August 1942, CNMI Covenant dates, Tuvalu colony end, Tripartite Convention date).
